go home, celebrate New Year's. Thank you very much.
- And mine?
442: And we'll return your charges to their place today.
443:
And if the cloakroom attendant turns up,
we might need you again?
444:
I didn't want to tell you, but today Bely—Docent—
escaped from the penal colony.
445:
Incredible, but true. It's dangerous for you
to stay like this.
446:
Maybe tomorrow? It's New Year's, after all,
and in their way they tried too.
447:
We live outside the city—it's unlikely
Docent can find us.
448:
All right, but don't take one step off the dacha!
Yes, we forwarded your letter
449:
to Sheremetyev's wife. Here's her reply.
Addressed to him.
450:
- You'll have lunch with us on the first, promise?
- We promise!
451:
Pity—such a good woman, and her father is
a fence, a speculator.
452:
Why are you yelling? Who allowed you out?
- He's here... A bad person.
454:
The New Year has come. I wish that in this
new year everything for you will be new.
455:
Anything can happen, but know this:
Wherever you are, wherever I am,
456:
I will always remember you,
and I will definitely find you.
457:
- And now... One moment...
- Where'd he go?
458: Who knows? You can't understand anything about him now.
459:
What's there to understand? He says he'll find you anywhere
and cut your throat.
461:
They say he slit Ryaboy's throat with a razor—snip, and bye-bye.
- Totally gone feral, the jackal.
462:
Who's come to see you? It's Ded Moroz,
he brought you gifts!
463:
- Fedya, come here. - What did I do?
- Come on, come on. Wear them in good health—house slippers.
464:
- What the hell do I need them for? I don't even have a home.
- You will. It's all ahead of you.
465:
- For now they'll come in handy in prison too. Wear them.
- All you do is croak.
466:
This is for you, Vasya... Gavrila Petrovich, this is for you.
- Thank you.
467:
- Pure wool.
- This is for you too.
470:
- What, do you have to get drunk like a pig?
- What else is there to do?
471: We could just sit and talk heart to heart.
472:
I'm not a prosecutor to talk heart to heart with you.
- We could play a game.
473:
Would you look at that! Found a sucker to play with you!
You've got nine aces in the deck.
474: Why does it have to be cards?
475:
Here's a good game—cities.
I say "Moscow,"
476:
and you, with the last letter "A"—Astrakhan.
And you, with "N"—Novgorod. Get it?
478:
Vorkuta.
Why? I did time there.
479:
- Good. And you, then—"A."
- Jambyl. - What's Jambyl got to do with it?
480: Because it's warm there. That's my home, that's my mother.
481:
Then let's play like this. I'll go out, you hide something,
I come back—I find it.
482:
- You'd better find our helmet.
- Shut up.
483:
- We'll hide it, and he'll be the one peeking through a hole?
- Why? You go out and hide it.
484:
And you watch so I don't peek.
Why me? Anything happens—it's Fedya right away.
485:
- I'll rip your mouth open, you filthy little bastard!
- Mouth, mouth...
486:
- Docent, were you ever little?
- I was.
487:
- Did you have a dad and mom?
- I did.
488: Why are you so mean? Why like a dog?
490:
- Came on my own.
- Ah. And you're here too.
491:
I was about to drop by, but I can feel it—
there's an ambush there.
492: Mityay, I need to hide out.
495:
- Sorry, doctor, for bothering you for nothing.
- It's fine.
496:
Give him some valerian, warm tea, and let him sleep.
- Thank you.
497:
- Does it hurt, Garik?
- It hurts, Vasya. Read it.
499:
"Hello, dear Dad! We found out
that you're in prison,
500:
and we were very happy, because we thought
you were dead."
501: Which bastard told that little Khmyr about Khmyr?
502:
"And Mom was happy too, because
when the letter came, she cried
503:
all day, and before that she said you were
a test pilot."
505:
"And I'm happy anyway that you're alive, because
Mom says
507:
Exactly! Weak-willed—stole the common money
and blamed it on the cabbie.
508: Beat it! I'll knock your horns off, radish!
510:
Aren't you ashamed! You're 40 years old,
half your life is already gone.
511:
What's behind you? What's in the present?
What's ahead?
512:
Darkness, filth, and nothing human!
Come to your senses while it's not too late. That's my advice.
513:
Docent, we gotta take off—
the lady doctor will squeal to the cops.
514:
- She won't. - Why?
- Because I did her in—razor to the throat...
515: she's in the well, you can go look.
516: What did I have? One year.
518:
How much for the kindergarten and the apartment?
Let's say ten!
520: And for a lousy fourteen years I'll put up with that viper?
521:
The one the old woman threw in the well?
Whatever you want, I'm going to the police.
523:
And you? You'll keep putting up with him
until you die, huh?
524: Vasya, I told him earlier: I've got a runny nose—and he...
525:
Enough with your runny nose, you're driving me nuts.
Come here...
527:
- What's going on?
- We're going to beat a rug.
528:
That's it, comrades. Finita la commedia.
First of all, I'm taking this off.
530:
I'll do my time and that's it. I'll quit!
Get a job.
531:
- As what? A watchman at your collective farm.
- Why a watchman?
532:
I can shovel snow, lay bricks, or be a translator—
I know English.
533:
If only we'd brought the hat too!
Who's Docent? A crook.
534:
- There are lots of crooks, but only one hat.
- If we brought the helmet, they'd cut our time.
535: Where'd he put it? Seems like we searched everywhere.
536:
Crook! Did I tell you I've got a runny nose?
And you: "Mouth, mouth."
537:
- Made me dive in that freezing cold!
- When did he make you dive?
538:
When they caught us. Remember? He says,
"I'm fishing," and you dive.
539:
- Wait—what did he say about fishing then?
- "I'm fishing in the ice hole,
540:
and you," he says, "Kosoy, can you swim?"
- He hid the helmet in the ice hole—that's it!
541:
Exactly! I remembered, bad person!
In the ice hole—in Malakhovka!
542:
Why didn't you say so? You lout! You could've left a note when you hanged yourself.
- Let's go.
543:
- And him?
- Nothing. Let them pick him up themselves. Carrying that hog. Let's go!
545:
- There's nothing there.
- It's there, at the bottom. You need to dive.
546:
Why me? Anything happens—it's Kosoy right away.
Vasya, tell him to go in himself.
547: I can't! It's cold, I'll get sick.
548:
- Just now he was hanging himself, now he's afraid of catching a cold!
- Fitness greetings!
550:
- Where's the boat station?
- Over there.
551: I'd stitch you up, but I haven't got time to mess with you!
552:
Now it's two pieces.
And there's one more at the dacha.
554:
- One!
- Well done, Fyodor Petrovich, well done!
555:
- Two.
- The more we turn in, the better.
